summary: L-4 cab built 1940 on War Creek Ridge in Okanogan County; used by the AWS in 1942, abandoned in the 1950s and now gone, with one footing left at the site.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s and gone; a 2020 visit recorded one footing of rock and concrete

access.note: Within Okanogan National Forest and reached on foot; no structure to visit. The seasonal gate on the access road was closed in June 2020.

visit.trail_note: Drive from Twisp west on Twisp River Road to War Creek Campground, then hike. The old ridge trail is fading; the 2020 visitor suggested going off trail up the hillside.

events.note: Used by the AWS to spot enemy aircraft in spring and summer; activated March 29 and deactivated September 19, 1942; winter use at the War Creek Guard Station
Abandoned in the 1950s (the sources give the decade only)

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence: no source gives the cab's size, height, builder or the exact year it was abandoned beyond 'the 1950s'. Willhite's page places the War Creek station in Chelan National Forest in one sentence, while firelookout.com and the record say Okanogan NF; not resolved, the story uses Okanogan. Willhite's photo captions are dated 1934, before the 1940 build; not explained by any source read. The Aircraft Warning Service is written as 'AWS' on the pages read; the story describes it without spelling it out. The 2020 visit date is inferred from the page's references to 2020 conditions. Access is marked public because the site is on National Forest land, but no source states public access directly.
